operator_path: Clone the exact baseline on Windows or Linux, locate every normative entry point, run offline documentation and contract checks, and observe deterministic rejection of a broken Schema fixture.
must_scope: Add deterministic documentation and JSON Schema validation scripts
Validate UTF-8, replacement characters, Markdown fences, local links, ADR status, JSON parsing, $id uniqueness, local $ref, and JSON Pointer resolution using only the Python standard library
Add positive and deliberately broken bootstrap fixtures for the checker
Add Windows and Linux GitHub Actions for offline documentation and contract checks
Synchronize baseline documentation affected by the checks
out_of_scope: Python package or runtime skeleton, pyproject.toml, or uv.lock
Ruff, Pyright, pytest, Hypothesis, or application unit tests
Pydantic authoring models or generated-model drift
Hermes Shim, HTTP server, database, LangGraph, Agent, browser, Git mutation, or provider behavior
Acceptance of Phase 00 or any later Slice
interfaces: Bootstrap documentation and Schema validation command contract
prohibited_actions: Edit src/ or add production behavior
Add pyproject.toml, uv.lock, runtime dependencies, or package code
Use public network or credentials in required checks
Commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, clean, or alter Git remotes, configuration, or hooks
Change accepted ADR semantics or expand Slice scope without a Contract Change Request

data: None: no runtime or Project data is created
migration: None: the repository has no runtime state
compatibility: Validation scripts and workflow must behave consistently on supported Windows and Linux runners
security: Checks are read-only, offline, bounded, and treat repository text as untrusted data
documentation: README, documentation map, policy links, Schema bootstrap note, and readiness audit remain synchronized

acceptance_criteria.observable_result: A clean clone exposes all required root entry points and every indexed local documentation link resolves.

All bootstrap Schemas parse, have unique $id values, and resolve every local or absolute $ref and JSON Pointer fragment to a declared Schema using only the Python standard library; full Draft 2020-12 meta-schema validation remains owned by slice-00-03.
A deliberately broken fixture is rejected with a stable nonzero exit and actionable bounded output.
The same offline check commands are configured for required Windows and Linux GitHub Actions jobs.
Validation reads repository data only, performs no network access, executes no repository-provided shell string, and emits no secret or Project content.
The Candidate changes no runtime or application path and contains no production behavior.

required_tests: Positive documentation and Schema baseline fixture
demonstration: From fresh Windows and Linux clones of the exact Candidate, run the documented offline commands successfully, then substitute the deliberately broken fixture and show deterministic rejection without modifying repository state.
required_evidence: Bounded command output and exit codes

risks.description: Cross-platform path or line-ending behavior causes the same baseline to validate differently.
risks.mitigation: Use pathlib and JSON Schema registry semantics, enforce repository line endings, and run identical commands on Windows and Linux.
risks.trigger: A required job disagrees with another platform for the same Git tree.

risks.description: The Slice expands into the Python package or Pydantic toolchain before its owning Slice.
risks.mitigation: Enforce path scope and stop on any required dependency or runtime code.
risks.trigger: Acceptance appears to require pyproject.toml, uv.lock, package code, or a new dependency family.

stop_conditions: Validation requires a new dependency family or public network access
Implementation requires runtime code or paths outside the permitted set
Accepted ADR semantics or observable Slice results must change
The Base SHA or approved Phase Plan changes
Required Windows and Linux behavior cannot be made equivalent
